verdict.rationale: Discord's developer platform supports OAuth2 with granular scopes (e.g. applications.builds.read, connections) and separate bot tokens with configurable permissions, which lets a developer issue least-privilege credentials for an app/bot that could act as an agent. However, there's no documentation specifically framing this for AI agents, no mention of short-lived/ephemeral credential issuance workflows tailored to autonomous agents, and no independent evidence of this being used for scoped agent credentialing in practice. Missing for 10: agent-specific credential provisioning docs, token lifecycle/revocation controls for autonomous use, and independent corroboration of least-privilege usage by AI agents.
